constraints.layout: Exactly n+1 nonempty lines: first line n m, then one explicitly signed integer +a_i or -a_i per line; 1<=a_i<=n. LF/CRLF and horizontal surrounding whitespace allowed, missing final newline allowed. Flattening or added blank rows rejected.
constraints.guarantee: At least one criminal c in 1..n yields exactly m true answers; parser rejects unsatisfiable instances.
constraints.output: Exactly n lines in speaker order, each Truth, Lie, or Not defined. Exact strings returned by answer; unique output is safe for token comparison, and review additionally enforces line layout.

oracle.algorithm: Count all negative statements and per-target signed balance. Candidate c is feasible iff negatives+balance[c]==m. A statement about an excluded target is always false for + and true for -. An included target is ambiguous with multiple candidates; with one candidate its sign determines Truth/Lie.
oracle.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) memory, exact integers
oracle.independentReference: Materialize the boolean truth vector separately for every possible criminal by interpreting each signed statement, retain vectors with exactly m truths, and classify columns using all/any. This does not use histogram/candidate logic.
oracle.brutePlan: Every signed assignment for n=1..4 and every m=0..n, checking all feasible instances; 300 fixed-seed additional n=5..40 cases. Independent truth tables also check every small authored pair and each supplied official/sample pair.
oracle.countMeaning: One assertion per feasible small instance comparing efficient oracle with independently materialized truth-table classifications. Does not include repeated runs, parser tests, additional supplied/generated pair checks, or independently validated problems.
